page.head.meta_content_1: I paid for the same purchase with nine crypto cards within minutes. A UAH 158 purchase cost $3.49–$3.82 before cashback. Fees, cashback and screenshots.
page.head.title_1: 9 crypto cards in Ukraine: one UAH 158 purchase
page.hero.p_1: I paid for the same hryvnia purchase with nine crypto cards. I compared actual debits, fees and cashback, and put together my conclusions for everyday spending and overseas subscriptions.
page.hero.p_2: Completed spend: 3.49 USDT. No cashback on USDT spending.
page.hero.p_4: About ${{SUBS_TOTAL}} of this goes to known subscriptions.
page.comparison.p_1: Compare debits, monthly cashback potential, or purchase costs after included cashback. Each card has its details and evidence.
page.comparison.p_2: Every card has a link without a referral code. My referral links are labeled separately; invitation bonuses are excluded from the ranking. Check the current terms when signing up.
page.comparison.p_3: Amounts are nominal USD equivalents. The cost with cashback uses the displayed cashback amount; BTC uses a fixed reference valuation. See the methodology for what the ranking includes.
page.comparison.summary_1: Compare all exact figures in a table
page.recommendations.h2_1: The choice depends on the payment
page.recommendations.p_1: I choose separately for purchases, bills, subscriptions and shared access.
page.recommendations.p_2: OKX has the lowest debit in this test. I keep a backup for bills: in my earlier Vega / RozetkaPay test, OKX and Bybit declined the payment, while Simple, Kolo and Solid accepted it.
page.recommendations.p_3: Solid for the displayed 3% cashback; payout still needs reconciliation. Simple for verified 1:1 Apple and ChatGPT payments. OKX also gave a favorable OpenRouter debit. Payment examples are in each card’s calculations.
page.recommendations.p_4: Solid showed the largest cash cashback for the test purchase. I estimate balance income separately within the cards: these are projections under current terms, not a measured APY ranking.
page.sources.p_1: Test amounts can be checked against the screenshots. I keep provider terms, my earlier experience and calculated models separate from measurements.

page.methodology.intro: The test is one 158 ₴ purchase on 09.10.2026. I assume 1 USDT ≈ 1 USDC ≈ $1 for comparison; card denomination, spending asset and internal settlement currency may differ.
page.methodology.debit: Debit: before balance minus after balance. Exceptions are USDT spent on the completed OKX screen, Bybit’s USDT debit in asset history, Trustee’s exact receipt and Solid’s Available to spend. Initial balances are kept separate from completed payments.
page.methodology.benchmark: The NBU rate on the test date was 44.8526 ₴/$, giving a $3.522649746… purchase equivalent. Deviation includes visible costs, not only FX spread. I do not add included fees twice.
page.methodology.included: I deduct displayed Solid $0.11 and COCA $0.03 before credit, Bybit’s 36 credited points at 0.002 USDT/point = 0.072 USDT under redemption terms, and Kolo / WhiteBIT BTC at a fixed valuation. Bybit point redemption into USDT is unverified. Trustee Points contribute $0 to the current cash calculation.
page.methodology.model: Potential assumes $1 000 of eligible purchases over a full month on the base or next tier, after the cap and annual fee / 12. It excludes FX, funding, categories, APY and token capital costs. COCA’s cap limits claiming rather than accrual. This is a terms-based model, not measured monthly profit.
page.methodology.btc: I include displayed Kolo and WhiteBIT BTC before crediting at a fixed $82976.035/BTC valuation. This is neither spendable USD nor a future payout rate; each card’s details contain the valuation and source.
page.methodology.precision: One small purchase and rounded balances limit ranking precision. Sub-cent differences may depend on rounding; fixed fees change results at larger amounts. An app status does not always prove card-network settlement.
page.sources.issuer_note: I used my confirmations, BIN lookups and public terms. OKX’s BIN databases conflict, so Bano remains provisional. WhiteBIT’s help page names JSC Hash Bank, while BIN lookups show Insbank; the reason is unresolved. A BIN database does not replace the individual card agreement.
sort.kolo_note: First 30 days: up to $20; then up to $10/month at 1%. EUR-card purchases over €100 hit the per-transaction cap. My card’s introductory-period eligibility is unverified.
programs.kolo.notes.2: Individual USD / EUR cards only; business and co-branded cards are excluded. No merchant-category restrictions. Refunds before payout reduce cashback. The app shows the highest rate across cards, while each earns its own rate. The potential ranking uses the introductory maximum of $20; this is neither a permanent 2% rate nor confirmed eligibility for my card’s introductory period.
sort.whitebit_note: Up to $25 after selecting up to 3 categories, with enough eligible spending. Subscriptions 10%, taxi / pets 5%; currently 0/3 active. This is a ceiling, not a payout forecast for the entire budget.

earning.title: Earning
earning.method_title: How I calculate Earning and total benefit
earning.method: With even spending, average balance = ($1,000 + $0) / 2 = $500. APR: $500 × rate × 30 / 365. For APY, I use the equivalent daily rate: $500 × 30 × ((1 + APY)^(1/365) − 1). The model does not reinvest income. If the source does not specify APR/APY, I show both estimates as a range of assumptions, not a guaranteed payout.
earning.assumptions: I assume a constant rate and eligibility of the entire average balance. Subscriptions paid early, deposits in installments, and time outside an eligible balance change the result. Estimates exclude taxes and unknown claim costs; each card lists its program’s limits.
earning.combined: I calculate total benefit as cashback + spendable income − FX, conversion, funding and tier fees. I subtract each tier fee once. Balance income is not attributed to the UAH 158 purchase and does not change its ranking. In this model, 5% a year covers only about 0.20% of the monthly budget; debit cost and cashback remain the main factors for UAH spending.
earning.cards.bybit.note: USDT Auto-Earn is enabled; Auto Deduction during payment is verified by the 3.6407 USDT redemption from Savings. This funded the purchase; it was not income. I use the USDT rate rather than the “up to 10.89%” banner; rate tiers and caps for larger balances are unconfirmed.
earning.cards.coca.note: Variable 5% APY on the USD banking balance; EUR earns no income. Funds remain available for payments, transfers, and withdrawals without locking. The Starter and Standard table says unlimited, but T&C section 4.1 mentions an unspecified tier cap and a possible 2% rate above it; this conflict is unresolved.
earning.cards.simple.note: Income accrues automatically on the card balance; claims start at 1 USDC. The rate is variable; caps and tiers for larger balances are unknown. I have not tested a payout; the screen does not establish whether this rate requires a referral code.
earning.cards.solid.note: USDC / USDT deposits receive soUSD: the token count stays constant while its dollar value grows with DeFi income. soUSD is not fixed at $1. Withdrawals are claimed to have no exit fee or waiting period, usually taking minutes. I have not tested deposits, withdrawals, or card transfers; minimums and network / conversion costs are unknown.
earning.cards.solid.prime_note: The limit is shared across all Savings vaults. Daily accrual, manual claims in soFUSE: a token payout excluded from the USD projection. Prime eligibility is in the cashback section; active Prime is unconfirmed and its fee is counted once.
earning.cards.solid.borrow_note: Credit works only with USD Yield: soUSD backs card spending without a Savings withdrawal. I have not tested borrowing or Credit payments. Without LTV, liquidation rules, and repayment costs I cannot calculate net benefit: interest and income use different bases, so simply subtracting rates is insufficient.
earning.cards.okx.note: OKX officially excludes Ukraine from USDG Rewards, so I exclude this income. The article covers yield, not USDG trading availability or cashback terms. USDG itself is also unavailable in my account; I found no other Earning option for the card balance.
earning.cards.kolo.note: I found no Earning option for the card balance; income is unconfirmed and excluded from the model. BTC cashback is counted separately.
earning.cards.trustee_plus.note: I found no Earning option for the card balance; income is unconfirmed and excluded from the model. Trustee Points have no confirmed cash value.
earning.cards.keyone.note: I found no Earning option for the card balance; income is unconfirmed and excluded from the model. Premium fee savings are counted separately.
earning.cards.whitebit.note: The app’s Auto-invest makes recurring crypto purchases (DCA); it is not balance income. Historical ROI figures without a period or methodology are neither APR/APY nor my income. I have no active plans; card-linked Earning is unconfirmed and excluded from the model.
earning.cards.coca.claim_note: Income requires a manual claim from $1, then becomes available in the banking balance. Cashback claim caps of $15 / $25 do not apply to APY. The test counter rose from $0.00005191 to $0.00007055: +$0.00001864. This is an observed increase, not proof of claim or withdrawal, or measured APY.
earning.cards.bybit.usdc_note: USDC: 5.42% APR → ≈${value0} under the same model if Auto-Earn is enabled; mine is off. USDT Daily Yields shows +0.0001 USDT, but I have not reconciled the period or payout, so it provides no measured APY.

cards.okx.funding: Funding via X Layer → OKX Pay: 10 → 10 USDT, with no separate card transfer. X Layer withdrawal: all 10 USDT received; OKX paid the fee.
cards.okx.experience: For me, it comes with restrictions in Ukraine: USDG is unavailable, so I miss out on its cashback and balance yield. Using USDT is convenient and fast; this card had the lowest debit before cashback in my test. Online acceptance is uneven: RozetkaPay declined my payment in the test. If USDG were available and acceptance were better, I would consider it as my main card.
cards.bybit.funding: Funding via Polygon → Funding Account: 10 → 10 USDT. The card uses this balance without a separate transfer. Withdrawals follow exchange rules; the withdrawal amount and fee were not recorded in this test.
cards.bybit.experience: Funding and withdrawals are straightforward. To me, the card feels like a wrapper around exchange accounts, which matters when choosing it. Viewing full card details requires 2FA each time, and that can be inconvenient. Cashback and yield on certain currencies in the exchange account are positives. Online acceptance is uneven: RozetkaPay declined my payment in the test.
cards.coca.funding: Funding Ethereum USDT → Base USDC: 10 → 9.969083. Base withdrawal: all 9.969083 USDC received, with no token deduction or user-paid gas.
cards.coca.experience: Convenient overall. There is a USD account funded with USDT or USDC, and a EUR account funded with EURC. Supported networks depend on the token. Withdrawals are fast, but only USDC or EURC via Base is available. There is cashback and yield on the USD account balance.
cards.keyone.funding: Funding Base USDT → USDC: 10 → 9.910683. Base withdrawal: all 9.910683 USDC received, with no token deduction or user-paid gas.
cards.keyone.experience: Funding with USDT or USDC incurs a fee. There is no cashback, and withdrawals are available only via Base. I found nothing particularly distinctive about this card.
cards.kolo.funding: Funding Arbitrum → Wallet: 10 → 10 USDT. Arbitrum withdrawal including an existing balance: 11.46 − 1 fee → 10.46 USDT received.
cards.kolo.experience: Interesting mainly for convenient funding and withdrawals with different assets, family sharing and cashback, although the rate is modest. Share Card works. I think it could be a good option for people in the euro area; I have not run a separate EUR spending test.
cards.simple.funding: Polygon funding: 10 USDT → displayed 9.98 USDC; exact credit unknown. Withdrawal via the Simple wallet → my Base wallet: 9.989909 USDC received, with no token deduction on either leg.
cards.simple.experience: Everything is simple. Almost. There are a few extra steps, but overall it is very convenient to use. It is a shame there is no cashback.
cards.solid.funding: Funding Arbitrum → Fuse: 10 → 9.997 USDT; direct Fuse: 10 → 10 USDT. Both deposits withdrawn via Fuse: all 19.997 USDT received; Solid paid the fee.
cards.solid.experience: Currently the most interesting card for me: high cashback with a fairly clear process for receiving it. Separate EUR payments recently became available. Funding and withdrawals are fast, with several routes. The inconvenience: when a purchase needs approval, I get no notification. I have to open card settings and find Approvals.
cards.trustee_plus.funding: Polygon → wallet funding: 10 + 1 USDT. Separate card transfer: 10 → 9.965114 USDT; minimum 10 USDT. Withdrawal required a USDC → USDT exchange and another 1 USDT deposit for the fee. Final review: 11.885677 − 1 fee → 10.885677 USDT; completion unconfirmed.
cards.trustee_plus.experience: The worst experience among these cards. Everything feels slow and inconvenient: high minimum amounts, fees, extra steps and waiting. After this test, I cannot recommend it.
cards.whitebit.funding: Main exchange balance credited with 10 USDT, with no separate card transfer. Plasma withdrawal including an existing balance: form shows 11.18 − 0.1 fee → 11.08 USDT; completion unconfirmed.
cards.whitebit.experience: To me, it is a wrapper around an exchange account. It is fairly expensive to use. Cashback offsets some costs, but not all.

page.faq.title: Quick answers
page.faq.0.question: Which crypto card should I use for UAH purchases?
page.faq.0.answer: OKX had the lowest debit before cashback in my test. For bills, I keep a backup: in my earlier test, RozetkaPay declined OKX and Bybit, while Simple, Kolo and Solid accepted the payment. One test does not guarantee the same result for other purchases.
page.faq.1.question: Does the displayed purchase cost include deposits and withdrawals?
page.faq.1.answer: No. The cost ranking compares the purchase debit; cashback mode subtracts the included cashback. I show deposit, withdrawal and conversion fees separately within each card; network costs depend on the network you choose. The total cost depends on the route and transfer amount.
page.faq.2.question: Is the included cashback already available to spend?
page.faq.2.answer: Not always. Some cashback is displayed after the purchase, but its payout is still unconfirmed. I value credited Bybit points at the documented redemption ratio without a verified redemption, and BTC at a saved fixed valuation. Each card calculation states the basis for its amount.
